 Follow Remote-Controlled Toy Cars Recalled Over Dangerous Batteries. What Parents Should Know
 Parenting Patch Staff Mon, November 16, 2026 at 6:30 AM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Kakgold recalled approximately 294 remote-controlled stunt vehicle toys over a potentially deadly battery ingestion hazard. BY: UNSPLASH Parents who bought remote-controlled toy cars off Amazon are now being advised to return them following a recall for potential battery-­related death risk. On November 12, the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) announced the recall of about 294 Kakgold 4WD stunt vehicle toys.
 Per the report , the remote controls contain button-cell and lithium-ion batteries that children can easily access.
 The products violate mandatory federal toy safety standards because the batteries are not adequately secured against children's access.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Swallowing a button-cell or coin battery can cause serious injuries, internal chemical burns and even death, making the recalled toys a potential danger to young children.
 Which Remote-Controlled Toy Cars Are Included in the Recall?
 The recalled Kakgold 4WD stunt vehicles feature lime green and blue bodies, black chassis and distinctive wheel designs. BY: UNSPLASH
 The recall affects Kakgold-branded 4WD stunt vehicle toys sold exclusively through Amazon.com between July and September 2026. The toys were sold for between $34 and $50 during the sales period.
 The recalled vehicles have a lime green and blue body, a black chassis and four black wheels with lime green trim and diagonal rollers. They also feature checkered patterns, an "X" design and the words "PRO" and "RACING" on the body.
 The recalled toy car's remote control contains accessible button-cell and lithium-ion batteries that pose a serious ingestion hazard to children. BY: UNSPLASH
 Parents can further identify the recalled products by checking for a white hang tag attached to the vehicle. The tag displays the warning "Do Not Twist the Shaft" in red lettering, accompanied by illustrations marked with red crosses.
 Advertisement Advertisement The recall specifically concerns the remote control, which contains button-cell and lithium-ion batteries that children can easily access.
 The products were manufactured in China and sold by Shenzhenshi Juteng Lechuang Technology Co., Ltd., doing business as Kakgold.
 Why Are the Batteries Dangerous to Children?
 Accessible button-cell batteries in children's toys and remote controls can pose serious ingestion hazards. BY: UNSPLASH
 Battery-cell injury can occur when small button-cell and coin batteries are swallowed. The CPSC reports that swallowed button-cell batteries can cause damaging internal burns and death.
 The risk is especially troubling because the batteries are small enough to be ingested accidentally, while the recalled remotes are not designed to prevent children from reaching the batteries, the agency said.
 Advertisement Advertisement The agency called the problem a violation of federal toy safety rules because the battery compartments don't provide enough protection for children.
 While the recall highlights significant safety concerns, the company has not yet received any reports of injuries or incidents related to the affected products.
 What Should Parents Do If They Own the Recalled Toy Cars?
 Parents should stop using the affected remote-controlled cars and contact Kakgold for instructions on obtaining a full refund. BY: UNSPLASH
 Parents who bought the affected Kakgold remote-controlled cars should stop using them immediately and contact the company for guidance on receiving a full refund.
 Consumers will be asked to write "RECALLED" on the product and email a photograph showing that the toy has been properly disposed of in the trash.
 Advertisement Advertisement Parents can follow these steps to address the recall:
 Stop using the toys: Immediately stop using the recalled vehicles and their remote controls. Do not allow children to play with them.
 Contact Kakgold: Email the company at kakrecall@outlook.com for information about obtaining a full refund.
 Follow the disposal instructions: Write "RECALLED" on the product as instructed by the company.
 Submit proof of disposal: Email a photograph showing the product has been properly disposed of in the trash to kakrecall@outlook.com.
 The CPSC urged consumers to dispose of button-cell batteries safely using local hazardous waste procedures. Parents can find additional information about the recall through the CPSC's official announcement. The agency has identified approximately 294 affected units under recall number 27-085.
